publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The multiple beam klystron amplifiers (MKA) (Korolev, 1968) ensure higher microperveance value of an electronic beam, a reduction of an operating voltage, expansion of a device bandwidth. Thus the overall efficiency and output power is increased and overall dimensions of the device are decreased (Sandalov et al., 1997). The physical processes which are going on in the MKA electron gun of are described, and the basic equations of computer code multi-beam electron gun-Moscow State University (MBEG-MSU) developed for the theoretical analysis of electron-optical systems are presented. The goal is developing of MBEG-MSU computer code that can run on PC computer and be useful of the CPU time and user friendly interface. With this purposes the fastest numerical methods are employed

articleTitle: Hot Resistance Studies on Tungsten/Rhenium Wire
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Tungsten/Rhenium alloy wire is the most common material used to produce heaters for dispenser cathodes. Performance variation may be attributable to a range of factors, including cold work and rhenium content variation. This paper investigates these two areas by analysis of resistance vs. temperature for a range of wire diameters and alloy concentrations. In addition, tensile testing of wire samples is investigated for comparison. Data is presented and discussed

articleTitle: Microwave Decomposition of Hydrogen Peroxide
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: In this paper, we have successfully demonstrated the feasibility of using microwaves to decompose H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> to produce dry steam (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O) and oxygen (O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) gas. Complex permittivity of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> was measured over a frequency range of 50 MHz to 20 GHz. Decomposition experiments were carried out at various sample configurations and different microwave power levels. Gaseous decomposition products were analyzed and oxygen evolution was monitored

articleTitle: The Forming Peculiarities of Intensive Electron Beams of the Millimeter Wave Radiations Sources
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: In this work an approach, which permits to minimize disturbing influence of the thermal beam electron velocities and to diminish thermal beam halo in a transmission channel by means of introducing optimum cathode magnetic-flow Psi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">kopt</sub> was offered

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband 140 GHz, 1 kW Gyro-Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The design and simulation results for a 1 kW, 140 GHz gyro-amplifier are presented. A bandwidth of over 4.5 GHz has been achieved in simulation with peak saturated gain of over 52 dB. The HE <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">06</sub> mode of a confocal cylindrical waveguide is chosen as the operating mode and distributed loss is employed via diffraction to stabilize the circuit. The amplifier will be capable of amplifying short pulses on the nanosecond scale

articleTitle: Reservoir Cathodes - Recent Development
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: We review recent work on reservoir cathodes both by our organization and by others. Reservoir cathodes differ from impregnated cathodes in that barium emissive materials are stored in a reservoir attached to, but separate from, the cathode matrix. A diagram of our miniature reservoir cathode is shown

articleTitle: Validation Studies for CHRISTINE-CC Using a Ka-Band Coupled-Cavity TWT
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: A CW Ka-band coupled cavity TWT, a CPI model VTA-6430A2, is under study at the Naval Research Laboratory, partly for the purpose of validating a large signal coupled-cavity simulation code, CHRISTINE-CC, and an equivalent Block model description, both now under development. The CC-TWT is voltage tunable over the range 28 to 30 GHz, with a rated output power of 500W, and an instantaneous bandwidth of 500 MHz. The simulation code used to model the performance is a coupled cavity version of the CHRISTINE code, originally written to simulate helix TWT's (Antonsen, 1997)

articleTitle: A New Vacuum Oscillator with Open Resonator
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: A microwave vacuum oscillator based upon parametric instability of linear electron oscillators in electromagnetic field of higher modes of open resonators (OR), having phase inversion along the electrons trajectories is suggested. The instability takes place for even harmonics of electron oscillations frequency in parabolic well. OR field increment was obtained and studied. Computer simulation of the OR field dynamics allowed to study time dependences of the OR field energy for various sets of main parameters. A new device may be applied for generation of terahertz electromagnetic signals

articleTitle: Investigation of Characteristics of High-Power Wide-Band Plasma-Filled Traveling-Wave Tubes (TWT)
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Development of plasma TWT which is the broadband amplifier of microwave oscillations with high power of output signal in a continuous operation mode is carried out in VEI. The purpose of this development is creation of technological installation of the microwave oscillation radiation with frequency sweeping and creation of the output high power amplifier cascade of ground station for space communication. Our experience in development of plasma TWT has shown that presence of plasma in the transit channel expands a working frequency band, increases efficiency and output power of the tube. We received the maximum working frequency band around the given frequency (in our case 2.45 GHz - the allowed frequency for technological applications) at the maximum coupling impedance. Plasma influence on the electromagnetic properties of CCC SWS was provided by means of special glow discharge tube input in the transit channel of the slow wave structure model

articleTitle: Beam Generation and Transport for a THz TWT
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: This paper describes research on the generation of a 10 keV, 50 × 300 micron elliptical electron beamfor a 650 GHz TWT amplifier.

articleTitle: 170 GHz, 2 MW Coaxial Cavity Gyrotron - Test of the RF output system for the first industrial prototype tube -
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The design of the optical (q.o.) RF output system for the first industrial prototype of the European 170 GHz, 2 MW, CW coaxial cavity gyrotron for electron cyclotron heating and current drive in ITER has been verified at low power level. Results of measurements with a high quality TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">34,19</sub>-mode generator are in good agreement with the design calculation and is presented in the following paper

articleTitle: Analysis and Simulation of a TM01-Mode Launcher for an Overmoded Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: A TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub>-mode launcher for an overmoded cylindrical waveguide has been designed, developed and analysed. It consists of a coaxial to cylindrical waveguide transition ending with a wheel type mode launcher inside a cylindrical waveguide and impedance matching of coaxial line to guide impedance is done through three step impedance transformer. The structure is modeled and simulated using a 3D numerical software HFSS. The analytical and simulated results for VSWR are found in close agreement with the experimental results

articleTitle: Preliminary Modeling and Simulation Results of a Megawatt HOM-IOT
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Summary form only given. The high order mode inductive output tube (HOM IOT) is enabling technology for the Navy's MW-class FEL due to its high efficiency, compactness, low cathode voltage and standby characteristics. The only HOM IOT ever built is CPFs VHP-8330A1 prototype. It was developed for the APT program; unfortunately APT was cancelled in favor of reactor-based technology. The prototype achieved 920 kW of power when operated in pulse mode; unfortunately testing both long pulse and continuous wave was not possible due to problems associated with deformation of the annular control-grid. Recent advances in multiple beam klystron (MBK) electron optics technology have taken place which allows us to remove the problematic annular control-grid and cathode segments used on the VKP-8330A prototype and replace them with multiple, conventional IOT spherical control-grids and cathodes. We examine the effect of this change on performance and determine the number of electron beams a given design [frequency] can accommodate. Preliminary modeling and simulation results of a HOM IOT operating at 500 MHz, 625 MHz and 750 MHz isshown. We also provide maximum output power levels, size, and weight estimates for tubes designed to operate at each of the above frequencies

articleTitle: 3-B Simulation of Magnetrons Having a Secondary-Emission Cathode Stimulated by Electrons from a Field Emitter
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The results are given of the 3-D simulation of the secondary-electro multiplication process in a magnetron with a cold secondary-emission cathode in which the primary electron sources are the blade-shaped field emitters. The application of the anode voltage pulse tandem is conducive to improving the efficiency and reliability of triggering the electromagnetic self-oscillation excitation in a magnetron oscillator, as the nanosecond radiation pulses are being generated

articleTitle: Design, Simulation and Scale Model Cold Test of a Sever for the Los Alamos 94GHz TWT RF Structure
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: LANL has developed a new vane loaded waveguide RF structure for a sheet electron beam TWT. It is common for all high gain TWT amplifiers to require a circuit sever to prevent oscillations. We have developed a preliminary sever design in our vane loaded waveguide RF structure. A scale model of the RF structure was used at 10GHz to test several sever geometries. The structure and sever were simulated using HFSS

articleTitle: Pulsed Mode TWT Phase Noise Reduction by Direct Sampled Voltage Ripple from Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: An efficient technique of phase noise reduction on TWT is introduced. The direct sampling of voltage ripple on each pulsed mode with voltage droop is achieved with a simple sub system which is independent of main microwave path. The compensation mechanism comprises of phase compensation with a microwave voltage controlled phase shifter to the input of TWT

articleTitle: Cathode Emission Characterization Improvement
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The dependence of thermionic emission upon both the cathode's emissive capabilities and the applied electric fields complicates the concise characterization of emission in a vacuum electron device. This article proposes a modest refinement to the technique, first introduced by Longo and later improved by Vaughan, for combining the Richardson-Dushman equation, the Child-Langmuir space-charge law, and the Schottky effect in order to accurately characterize emission over a wide range of temperatures. The proposed refinement adds factors to account for the change in device geometry due to thermal expansion

articleTitle: Electron Beam Transverse Waves and Microwave Electronics
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: This report includes the discussion of the physics principles and technology of the following non-traditional devices: cyclotron wave protectors, low-noise cyclotron wave parametric amplifiers, narrow-band controlled CWESA-filters, high power circularly polarized travelling wave tubes (CPTWT), high power cyclotron wave converters, klystrons with combined interaction (KCI), and cyclotron wave phase shifters

articleTitle: Output Analysis of a Circular Horn Antenna: Higher Order Modes
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: An antenna is usually designed to produce a desired radiation far-field pattern in various directions. Horn antennas are widely used in the outputs of high power microwave tubes. We have created a 3-D circular horn antenna model by HFSS and calculated the output properties for the four important modes TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>, TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0l</inf>, TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf>, and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">03</inf>. We can use the HFSS code to find out some important parameters for the horn antenna, include the peak directivity and peak gain.

articleTitle: Shunt Impedance of the MBK Cavities
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: There are a lot of kinds of multiple beam cavities used in klystron amplifiers. Ring, classic cylindrical and multiple barrel cavities have been researched using CST Microwave Studio 5.0 simulation code. Shunt impedance of klystron cavities determines the efficiency of interaction of electron beam with EM field. So R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sh</inf>/Q values of cavities of interest are considered.

articleTitle: Simulated Impact of Non-Linear Memory Effects on Digital Communications in a Klystron
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The results of passing digital communications signals through a 1-D physics-based klystron model are presented and compared to the series block model. Nonlinear memory effects are shown to be important at high data rates near saturation

articleTitle: Bandwidth Extension of an S-band, Fundamental-Mode Eight-Beam Klystron
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: We present the design of a five-cavity, broadband, high-power multiple-beam klystron (MBK) operating in S-band. The MBK uses a 32 A, 45 kV eight-beam electron gun as presented in K. T. Nguyen et al. (2004) whose design has been successfully tested in a previous narrowband MBK circuit stated in K. T. Nguyen et al. (2004) and D. K. Abe et al. (2005). The circuit was optimized using the 3D particle-in-cell code MAGIC; the predicted performance includes a 3-dB bandwidth of 6.7%, peak power of ~600 kW and a gain of 33 dB. This circuit performance represents a three-fold increase in the bandwidth-power product relative to our previous circuit

articleTitle: Comparisons Between Fundamental and Higher Order TM Modes in Microwave Cylindrical and Coaxial Cavity of Klystron
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: In this paper, we calculate the parameters of typical transverse magnetic (TM) modes of microwave cavity; the fundamental modes (FM) and higher order modes (HOM). Calculations show that the TM <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">010</sub> mode of cylindrical cavity has an advantage of high characteristic impedance and drawback of small cavity size, and the TM <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">010</sub> and TM <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">310</sub> in cylindrical coaxial cavities have advantages of large cavity cross-section and some nearly equal parameters as Q-factor, frequency F and characteristic impedance Z. The results show agreement with the simulations

articleTitle: Design and Initial Testing of Omniguide Traveling-Wave Tube Structures
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: We propose to use the photonic band gap (PBG) structures for the construction of a traveling-wave tube (TWT) at W-band. The development of wide-band mm-wave TWT amplifiers is underway at Los Alamos National Laboratory. A TWT would present a wide bandwidth source for remote mm-wave spectroscopy. PBG TWT structures have great potential for very large bandwidth and linear dispersion. In addition, being cheap to fabricate, the PBG structures enhance the commercial transferability of the W-band TWT technology.

articleTitle: High Thermal Conductivity Aluminum Nitride for High Power Microwave Windows - An Update
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: We have undertaken an extensive study to determine and to control the factors to reduce the loss tangent of AlN to match those of Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2 </sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and BeO (tan5 equiv 0.0005) without adversely affecting its thermal conductivity, dielectric strength, and mechanical strength

articleTitle: Experiment of TWT Chaos Central Frequency Fast-and Continuously-Tuning System
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: We have carried out the TWT experiment with different feedback level and external signal to generate corresponding chaos output. When the external signal frequency is beyond the feedback filter, the "duplicated" branch and chaos amplitude will increase with the external signal amplitude, and will suppress the generation of delay feedback chaos. Experimental results agree well with theoretical analysis and computer simulation results. Details of the experiment are discussed in the conference

articleTitle: A 1 kW Microwave Power Module for Pulsed Radar
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: A computer-aided design methodology was used to develop an efficient vacuum electron device and electronic power conditioner for use in a microwave power module. The MPM has been built, tested, and delivered to the customer for integration into a developmental radar. Comparisons between predicted and measured values are reported at the conference

articleTitle: Study on Photonic Crystal Cavity for Harmonic Multiplying Gyroklystron using Axis-encircling Electron Beam
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Photonic band structure is employed in the second stage using the concept of photonic bandgap (PBG) to overcome mode competition and the limited beam propagation in harmonic multiplication devices. When the line defect is made inside of PBG structure it works as cavity excited by single mode. If suitable PBG condition for the cyclotron maser instability with higher beam harmonics is found, gyroklystron can be operated in single high order mode without mode competition. The numerical simulation using MAGIC code is carried out in two-stage harmonic multiplying gyroklystron

articleTitle: An Examination of Magnetic Fields from Cathode Heaters
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Presented here are analytic results obtained using Field Precision's Magnum FEA code of the DC magnetic field at an X-axis line 0.078 inches (2 mm) from a planar emitter face and at a Z-axis line at a point on the circumference. Results are presented in relative terms, as the analyses assume a specific current and wire length, items which are, from one heater design to another, not generally interchangeable. Also presented is a subjective yet practical comparison of some of the strengths and weaknesses of each coil

articleTitle: Generation of Electromagnetic Oscillations by Electron Beam in Open Resonator: 3D Modeling
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Feasibility evaluation and theoretical consideration of a vacuum oscillator as presented in K. A. Lukin (2004) and K. A. Lukin (2006) has been carried out on the basis of 3D modeling of electron oscillators motion and their interaction with electromagnetic field of open resonator (OR). A new device may be applied for generation of millimeter and sub-millimeter (terahertz) electromagnetic waves

articleTitle: Monitoring and Data Acquisition of CFA Processing Parameters
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Processing of the SFD-262 and SFD-268 cross-field amplifiers has been performed for set periods of time and under specific operating parameters. CPI/BMD has implemented a process monitoring and data collection system to provide real-time assessment of the condition of CFAs during the age and burn-in processing. The goal of this activity is the customization of the age and burn-in process for individual CFAs and the hastening of processing

articleTitle: The Effects of Synthesis Process on Aluminate Emitters Thermionic Properties
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: This paper describes some different synthesis methods of barium-calcium aluminate to be used as a thermionic emitter. It is also investigated thermionic emission measurement techniques to characterize the impregnated cathodes under development. A Pierce type electron gun is scaled up to match the electron gun designed with the desirable beam parameters like applied voltage and cathode emission current density in order to determine the space-charge current limit

articleTitle: Space Charge Effects on Thermionic Emission: the Knee of the Transition from TL to FSCL Operation
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: We study the space charge effects on thermionic emission via a self-consistent approach. The Richardson-Dushman equation, corrected for the Schottky effect and the Poisson's equation including relativistic effects are solved iteratively. The knee of the transition curve from TL to FSCL operation is obtained self-consistently.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Complex Dielectric Permittivity Behavior of Composites based on Al2O3/AIN and Precursor-Derived-SiC in the 1 MHz 18GHz Frequency Range
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The current research involves the synthesis of microwave-absorbing ceramic-based composites which exhibit a controllable variation in complex dielectric permittivity with respect to frequency. This study focuses on the synthesis and dielectric analysis of both porous and fully dense Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-precursor-derived-SiC, as well as AlN-precursor-derived-SiC composites, obtained by applying various types of high temperature treatments to as-pyrolyzed porous composites

articleTitle: Ka-Band CCTWT Development at L-3 Electron Devices Division
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: In describing the development and measured results to date, this paper discusses the design process which led to a nearly fully compliant prototype on the first build. A priori design code predictions were shown along with the measured hardware performance. In the interest of continuous improvement, lessons learned are also be given. These include use of design codes to help resolve subsequent manufacturing issues which were not anticipated in the initial design process

articleTitle: Development of a I-J Band High Power Mini TWT
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: This paper describes the development of a 6 to 18.5 GHz active bandwidth; 115-175 watt CW high power mini TWT suitable for commercial and EW applications. This device has 35 dB small signal gain at the band edges to achieve low noise power density. The TWT mechanical envelope is a compact, 9.6 inches package. The typical prime power consumption is less than 580 watts with a three stage depressed collector

articleTitle: Preliminary Design of a High Power, High Efficiency, Ka-Band Complex Cavity Gyrotron Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: In this paper, basing on a particle in ceil (PIC) simulation code, the beam-wave interaction of a Ka-band complex cavity gyrotron with gradual transition is studied. The effects of cavity dimension, electron beam parameter and operating magnetic field on the electron efficiency, output power and operating stability are analyzed. The results show that an output power of 716kW, a high interaction efficiency of 60.2% and good stability are predicted at 33.4GHz for the complex cavity gyrotron driven by a 70kV, 17A electron beam with a pitch angle of 1.5

articleTitle: High Voltage Compatible Micromachined Vacuum Electronic Devices with Carbon Nanotube Cold Cathodes
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Previously, Bower et al. [1] demonstrated a microfabricated vacuum microtriode with an integrated carbon nanotube field emission cathode. One of the main limitations of the microtriode was the inadequate device insulation which suffered from leakage currents and electrical breakdown at fewer than 200 Volts. Here, we report similar micromachined vacuum electronic devices fabricated to withstand voltages in excess of 1000 Volts. The DC electrical characteristics of a microtriode were obtained at grid and anode voltage levels significantly higher than previously reported. The field emission performance of the MPECVD grown carbon nanotube cold cathode is described Implications for future on-chip microfabricated vacuum electronic devices will be discussed.

articleTitle: A 6.6 GHz Monotron with a Coaxial Bragg Reflector
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: A coaxial line periodically loaded by circular disks on the inner conductor is specifically designed to act as Bragg reflector to prevent r-f fields from leaking out of a 6.6 GHz monotron Design criteria to ensure a stopband as wide as possible are presented and a discussion is given on how band gap width, center frequency, and reflectivity arise from the geometry of the periodic structure.

articleTitle: Outgassing of FED Under Operation
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: In this paper, the outgassing of field emission display(FED) was studied using vacuum chamber and FED panel. The gas was measured with a quadrupole mass spectrometer(QMS), and the mean gas outgassed from the FED panel is CO when the device is working at about 1000V.

articleTitle: The Rigorous Excitation Equations for the Arbitrary-irregular Waveguides with Finite Conduction of the Wall
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: On base general theory for the irregular waveguides the rigorous excitation equations for the arbitrary-irregular waveguides with finite conduction of the wall for the relativistic TWT and gyrotrons theory were obtained

articleTitle: High Power CW BeO Block Brazed Copper Helix TWT
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The unique copper helix TWT is developed for power CW operation in applications of communication, electronic warfare, and high power microwave test equipment. The superior thermal conductivity of copper allows substantially efficient amplification over broadband. Three BeO blocks per turn are brazed into their both sides of contact to increase heat dissipation. This paper introduces merits of helix material selection, block dielectric supports and their brazing which entails in rugged structure and high power operation

articleTitle: Experimental Study on 100MW X-band Relativistic Backward Wave Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: An rippled-wall RBWO is operated at the beam voltage of 250∼400kV and current of 2.1∼3.4 kA using the 130nsec, single shot using Seoul National University's Electron Beam Accelerator(SEBA). SEBA produces a hollow beam of 19.2mm-outer radius, 0.7-thickness guided by an axial magnetic field of 1.7∼3.4 Tesla. The uniform ripple has a period of 11mm, mean radius of 14mm and ripple amplitude of 2mm. A single cavity-type reflector which excites a TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf>mode and cutoff a TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>mode at the operating frequency is chosen. Microwave generated by the RBWO is radiated through an 11cm-diameter horn antenna. The radiation pattern of TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>mode is measured by fluorescent lamps. The measured and simulated angle of radiation is about 14.9 degree and 13.1 degree, respectively. 110MW microwave was measured at the operating diode voltage of 330kV, the beam current of 2.8kA with the guiding magnetic field of 3.0 T. Efficiency of 12% is obtained by both numerically and experimentally. A typical 20 nsec microwave pulse is measured in the preliminary experiment. The frequency of 11.8GHz is measured by a heterodyne method.

articleTitle: Transportable, High-Power THz Source
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Advanced energy systems is developing electron beam based terahertz (THz) sources ranging from man-portable, moderate power devices to transportable high power devices. This paper focuses on the development of a high power source suitable for use from a standard vehicle

articleTitle: A Field Emission Based Ka-Band Millimeter Wave Generator
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The Ka-band millimeter wave is generally discussed, and there have been many inventions and applications of it. We propose a vacuum electronic device based on field emission mechanism for the generation of Ka-band millimeter waves. The verification of the generation of millimeter waves has been done using a 2D finite-difference time-domain particle-in-cell code MAGIC (developed by MRC Co., VA, US). A resonance at about 35 GHz is found after doing fast Fourier transformation by observing the output power in time domain.

articleTitle: Study of the Charge Deposition on the Insulator Walls in a Field Emission Display Panel
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The field emission display panel has been regarded as one of the promising flat display panel in the future(Burden et al., 2003 and Talin et al., 2001). It is well known that the charge deposition on the insulator walls in a FED can change the distribution of the electric field and the emission performance of the cathode obviously. This paper simulates the movements of the primary electrons emitted from the cold cathode. Then, the secondary electron emissions from the insulator wall are also estimated. Finally, the influence of the charge deposition is studied

articleTitle: Study on Ballistic Bunching in Frequency Multiplying Distributed Interaction Gyroklystron Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: We re-classify this two-stage and highly tapered gyro-device as distributed interaction two-cavity gyroklystron since this device has a finite interaction length at each operating frequency in a highly tapered waveguide. Here the ballistic bunching theory previously driven is used for the estimation of the maximum bunching distance for each operating frequency. The third harmonic multiplying scheme is applied to two-stage tapered waveguides with a rectangular cross-section. The large-orbit electron beam is adopted operating at the beam voltage and current of 30kV and 1A, respectively. Theoretically predicted maximum bunching length is compared with the drift length from the Lareg-Signal-Theory code simulation. And they are compared with the interaction length of the circuit

articleTitle: Limiting Currents in Magnetically Focused Intense Relativistic Beams Filled with Background Plasma
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The intense relativistic beam propagation through drift tubes filled with background plasma is investigated. The beginning portion of the electron beam pulse creates an ion channel in drift tubs. The self-consistent differential equations, which describe the laminar-flow equilibria state in magnetically focused relativistic beams with ion channel, are presented. By solving these equations, the limiting current and the externally applied magnetic field can be obtained in solid beams and hollow beams.

articleTitle: Numerical Determination of Interaction Impedance on Birdsall Slow-Wave Structures
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: This paper presents the results of the initial stage in the development of a computer code based on the tangential vector finite element method for computing the dispersion and the interaction impedance characteristics of a Birdsall type slow-wave structure (SWS). This code has been developed in order to consider the coupling waveguides effect on the interaction impedance

articleTitle: Recent Results in GYCOM/IAP Development of High-Power Gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The paper presents the latest achievements in development at IAP/GYCOM of MW power level gyrotrons for fusion installations. During last years several new gyrotrons were designed and tested at IAP/GYCOM. Among them are the new version of 170 GHz gyrotron for ITER and multi-frequency (105-140 GHz) gyrotrons for Asdex-Up. All these gyrotrons are equipped with diamond CVD windows and depressed collectors. Corresponding transmission line components and dummy loads were tested at high power of microwaves in long-pulse or CW regimes

articleTitle: Improve the Emission Stability with Large Current from a CNTs Cathode
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Field emission characteristic and stability of a carbon nanotubes(CNTs) cathode have been studied by testing the emission current at different levels. By monitoring the emission I-V curves, we can obtain a relative stable maximum current from a CNTs cathode, after reaching the maximum current, the emission current fluctuate seriously and sparking can be seen at the site of emission. From the experimental results, the causes of emission instability and sparking is concluded and the influence of the sparking and ion bombardment on the emission performance of a CNTs cathode is obtained.

articleTitle: Optimization of Normally-On Driving Under-gate CNT FED
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Double cathodes field emission display is proposed and the structural and electrical parameters are optimized in this paper. The calculation and experimental results shows that this structure can achieve good uniformity and high luminance

articleTitle: W-band Single-Anode MIG for Gyro-TWT
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: A coherent microwave and millimeter wave generation from fast-wave gyro-devices are attractive due to their high power handing capability. They have many applications such as plasma generation and heating, high gradient particle accelerators, and material processing. In the fast-wave gyro-devices, since the beam-wave interaction takes place between a transverse electric field of a guided wave and an electron transverse momentum, producing a high quality gyrating electron beam with a low velocity spread is a critical issue in the design of high performance gyro-devices. Different types of electron guns producing the gyrating electron beam with a large transverse momentum have been studied in many countries. The double-anode and single-anode magnetron-injection-guns (MIG) are commonly used. Due to the mechanical complexity of the double-anode MIG , however, the single-anode MIG which does not include the modulating anode seems attractive for use in practical devices. This paper describes studying on a single-anode MIG which produce a high quality gyrating electron beam. The design is based on analytic trade-off equations. And computer simulation uses the electron trajectory code-EGUN. The electron gun is used for a W-band, TE <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> gyro-TWT amplifier which required to producing a small orbit electron beam

articleTitle: Microwave Pulse Compression using Helically Corrugated Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Cylindrical waveguide with a helical corrugation on the inner surface has proven an effective dispersive medium for the compression of smoothly frequency modulated microwave pulses. This paper presents the results of experiments where ∼5.6kW, X-band (8.0GHz to 12.5GHz), microwave pulses of 80ns duration and 5% frequency modulation were compressed into 1.5ns pulses with 25 times higher peak power.

articleTitle: Effect of the External Coupling of Cavities on the Stability and Output Power of a Relativistic Magnetron
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Thus, the results of our investigations show that the external coupling of cavities in a relativistic magnetron significantly influences on the spectral and energetic characteristics of the oscillations. The original configuration of the coupling circuit is proposed, based on the scheme with common dissipative elements. This significantly improves the output microwave radiation signal parameters. One can expect that using a coupling channel with many radiators will make possible to create stable, ultrahigh-power, high-directivity radiation sources

articleTitle: Simplified Methodology to Evaluate Effect of Backscattered Electrons in Gyrotrons with Depressed Collectors
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: In gyrotrons with depressed collectors, some backscattered electrons go towards the RF cavity. Those reaching the cavity reduce the interaction efficiency and add excess heating load in a sensitive area; others are reflected back due to mirror effect. Mitigating the effects of backscattered electrons is critical for high power gyrotrons such as are needed for fusion research. This study provides a simplified method for evaluating which backscattered rays will reach the RF cavity, thus enabling comparisons of design options. An adiabatic approximation is used in the high field region in the vicinity of the RF cavity

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Field Distribution in Matched Intervals of Periodically-irregular Waveguides for Gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: In this paper, T-functions technique and finite element method numerical experiments were provided for TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0i</sub> modes of matched intervals of periodically-irregular waveguides with the account of cut-off modes. The forward and backward wave components interaction, as well as modes conversion, causes complex spatial distribution of the waves. The considered variants specify that the distributions do not match a second-order periodic condition as it was considered earlier. In all considered variants the waveguide intervals are impedance matched at the end sections

articleTitle: Rapid Startup In Magnetrons Using The Transparent Cathode
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The transparent cathode is a novel cathode design intended to provide rapid startup in pulsed, relativistic magnetrons (Fuks and Schamiloglu, 2005). The transparent cathode consists of separate longitudinal metal strips arranged on a cylindrical surface that act as electron emitters. The cathode may also contain a center conductor to provide mechanical support for the cathode strips

articleTitle: Controlled Porosity Cathodes Using Sintered Tungsten Wires
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Sintered tungsten wires provide a unique technique for creating controlled porosity dispenser cathodes. This research is investigating the relationship between sintering time and temperature on the porosity. A reservoir cathode using this technique is currently being designed and built

articleTitle: The Effect of Non Uniform Permanent Magnet Material on Transverse Fields in Periodic Permanent Magnet Focused Traveling Wave Tubes
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Data will be presented that demonstrates the effect of using uniform vs. non uniform magnetic material. Non-uniform magnetic material will be produced by "knocking" the individual magnets down from a range 18-20% higher than nominal gauss. Normal processing requires a "knockdown" range 0-5%. Individual magnets will be tested for circumferential variation. Tube performance will be measured for both uniform and non-uniform magnet PPM stacks

articleTitle: The Simplest Ubitron in Crossed Fields
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: We present the simplest type of an M-type ubitron in the form of a magnetically insulated coaxial diode with a cathode consisting of N individual longitudinal strips (explosive electron emitters) periodically arranged on an imaginary cylindrical surface mounted coaxially within a pipe. In spite of the simple design the operation of this device is not easily predicted, although we can definitely state that in the ubitron, as in the RPM, azimuthal recurrence provides inner feedback that leads to an absolute instability in the electron sheath-electromagnetic field interacting system; in other words, the ubitron can operate as an oscillator. The suggested oscillator can be interesting owing to its simple design and simple control of characteristics of radiation (with single frequency radiation as well as multi-mode one) by variation of the value and direction of the guide magnetic field

articleTitle: New and Improved Emission Models in the Finite-Element Gun Code MICHELLE
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: We continue to research and develop better emission models for gun codes. We describe our recent efforts to improve the thermal aspects of space-charge-limited emission, the transition from temperature-limited emission to space-charge-limited emission, and photoemission

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of a Photoemission Model for End-to-End Beam Simulations and Custom Photocathode Designs
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: This paper outlines the experimental techniques used to validate a photoemission model applied to metals with sub-monolayer alkali coatings. Essential features of the model are highlighted and its results are compared to experiment. Cesium was deposited in-situ on tungsten and silver polycrystalline substrates while quantum efficiency (QE) was measured as a function of surface coverage and other parameters. Good qualitative agreement with theory is demonstrated and significant differences in quantitative comparisons are addressed.

articleTitle: Test Results for a 19 kW, 1497 MHz Klystron for Accelerators
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: A 1497 MHz, 19 kW CW klystron for driving accelerators, and initial test results are described

articleTitle: LaB6-Based Gun Brightness vs Cathode Life
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Among commercially available cathodes, LaB6 seems to be the only one whose dimensions are changing considerably during its lifetime. Changing cathode geometry affects near-cathode field, emission current density, and, ultimately, its brightness. We report modeling results for the LaB6-based gun major parameters dependence on cathode changes during its lifetime

articleTitle: Reduction of Noise in Strapped Magnetron by Electric Priming using Anode Shape Modification
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Noise reduction in a 2.45 GHz strapped magnetron oscillator is experimentally demonstrated by electric priming using anode shape modification. The sideband noise are reduced by about 15 dB at the nominal operating current and 28 dB at the start-oscillation current due to electron prebunching into the π-mode resulted from the modulation of the drift velocity of the electron using the azimuthally periodic electric field. In this experiment, a 4.3kV and 330mA half-wave rectified input power is employed.

articleTitle: The Determination of Tape Helix Cold Test Parameters Using Fourier and Convolution Techniques
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: A program was written to predict cold test parameters of helix traveling wave tubes. Parameters such as dispersion, interaction impedance, and phase velocity can be obtained in that the flexibility of the program allows for quick simulations compared to commercial CAD packages.

articleTitle: Photoelectron Emission and Secondary Electron Emission Characteristics of Cesiated p-type GaN
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The emission characteristics of a cesiated p-type GaN sample are examined as a function of surface treatment, time following cesiation, and sample heating. The yield and energy distribution of both photoemitted electrons and secondary electrons are examined and correlated with the GaN surface properties

articleTitle: Recent Developments to TWTCAD Integrated Framework
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Recent developments to TWT Integrated Framework, a 2D modeling and simulation code suite for traveling wave tube, are presented. Two codes, UESTCPPM and UESTCDB, are added to TWTCAD. Existed another four codes are improved. TWTCAD is applying and validating in microwave industry

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis the Performance of Field Emission Display with Secondary Electrons Emission
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: In this paper, we calculated and compared the performance of three different structures of CNT-FED: a normal triode structure, a double-gate structure, and a structure with insulator channel. By calculating the electrical field and the electron trajectories, we found that the normal triode structure is easy to induce pixel-pixel interference; while the double-gate structure subtract the anode current because of the interception of the second gate. In the structure with insulator channel, the disadvantages mentioned above can be avoided. Furthermore, when the cathode has some defects, the uniformity of the anode current can be improved because of the secondary electrons generated at the surface of the insulator wall

articleTitle: Milliamp-Class, Back-Gated, Triode Field Emission Devices Based on Free-Standing, Two-Dimensional Carbon Nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: In this presentation we discuss recent results using carbon nanosheets (CNS) as the field emission source in a back gated device for high current applications

articleTitle: Application of the Finite-Element MICHELLE Beam Optics Code to RF Gun Modeling
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: RF guns and density modulated guns that encompass photocathodes and inductive output tube sources are difficult to model but continue to be at the forefront of solutions to many applications. Modeling these density-modulated beam sources requires a high degree of computational mesh resolution to resolve geometrical features, or simply fine spatial scale phenomena. This paper presents the application of the MICHELLE code to such devices

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Genetic Algorithm for Optimizing Dispersion and Coupling Impedance in Helix TWTs
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Optimization techniques have been used in traveling wave tubes design for the slow-wave circuit phase velocity taper and collector stages (Wilson, 2001; Chevalier et al., 2003). In the slow-wave circuit design, the objective function aims to minimize the difference between dispersions versus different frequency, and maximize the on-axis interaction impedance in a specified bandwidth. This is a double-objective optimizing problem. Unfortunately, the objective functions are conflicting. The small difference between dispersions comes with the decrease of interaction impedance. The single-objective optimization, therefore, is not suitable to pose this problem. However, to our knowledge, these multi-objective optimization techniques have not been applied to general slow-wave circuit design until now. The expression of evaluating interaction impedance in the sheath helix model was also presented

articleTitle: Estimation of Cold Characteristics for Fundamental-Mode MBK Cavities
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: We describe the development of simple formulae to accurately estimate the R/Q's in single-gap, fundamental-mode MBK cavities and to describe their sensitivity to radius and frequency. These equations can be very useful in the initial design process and can lead to robust cavity designs that are relatively insensitive to manufacturing tolerances

articleTitle: Installation of a Getter Vacuum Pump in Cathode-Anode Region of a High-Power Klystron Amplifier - Propose and Feasible
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The possibility to install a getter vacuum pump and its feasible in the anode of a high-power klystron amplifier is investigated in order to decrease of the pressure in the gun and consequently increasing its lifetime. The study is conducted using a 1.3 GHz, 100 A and 240 kV high-power klystron with five reentrant coaxial cavities, assembled in a cylindrical drift tube 1.2 m long. This work takes into account the specific conductance of components of gun and all important gas sources, like the degassing of the drift tube, the cavity walls, the cathode, the anode, and the collector, as well the position and pumping speed of the getter vacuum pump in anode region

articleTitle: Output Horn Antennas Profile Optimization for Far Field Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: On base general theory for the irregular waveguides (Kurayev et al., 2005) and horn antennas on E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub>-waves (Kurayev et al., 2005) the following variants horn antennas with irregular profiles optimized for far field radiation pattern (for antenna gain factor) were obtained

articleTitle: University Training of Tube Engineers, in the US and Abroad
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Approximately 30 years ago, it became apparent to the US tube industry that new engineering hires were not receiving specialized training in vacuum electronics because most or all universities had dropped related courses from their curricula. Twenty years earlier, the microwave tube industry was hiring engineers with PhD and Master's degrees from Stanford, University of California and MIT, who had actually built tubes in the university laboratories, tested them, and published papers on their work. These engineers, the pioneers in our industry, were approaching middle age in the 70s, and the schools they had graduated from were were no longer interested in microwave tubes. The US military developed similar concerns about this situation since the Cold War was at its peak and the DoD depended on the tube industry for electronic warfare components

articleTitle: Small-Sized X-Ray Tube with the Field Electron Emitter on the Base of Carbon Nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Field emitters on the base of carbon nanotubes can be used in various electron vacuum devices. We describe the construction and parameters of a prototype of an X-ray tube with the carbon nanotube field emitter. The X-ray tube is a glass device 40 mm long and 16 mm in diameter

articleTitle: Influence of Attenuator on the Performance of the Helix TWTs
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: On the basis of the 1D CHRISTINE, under the condition of attenuator considered, that is, its RF (Radio Frequency) characteristics including attenuation constant, phase propagation constant and interaction impedance taken into account, in the meantime, two different attenuation models set up, the nonlinear properties of beam-wave interaction in the helix TWTs (Traveling Wave Tubes) were analyzed, and the simulation results were compared with both conventional theory and experimental measurements under single signal excitation. The compared results clearly show that it is necessary to consider completely the attenuator's RF characteristics to accurately evaluate the helix TWT performances, especially in the small signal gain and AM/PM conversion.

articleTitle: Optimization of Multistage Collectors Using the MICHELLE Code Within the Analyst Modeling Framework
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Using the MICHELLE gun and collector code linked to the analyst finite-element modeling package, we have investigated the use of direct-search and statistical optimization strategies in the design of depressed collectors. Results of our work on an idealized device show that substantial improvements in efficiency can be realized using these methods

articleTitle: Mode Selectivity in Multiple-Beam Klystrons
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: We present a general method for calculating the coupling coefficients of multiple beamlets of an arbitrary geometry to resonator fields having arbitrary transverse distribution. To demonstrate the effectiveness of this method, we consider the specific case of an MBK cavity operated in the high-order TM4,1 mode and show the effect of device parameters on the calculated coupling coefficients of the operating mode and two nearest parasitic modes.

articleTitle: Tuning Characteristics of Reentrant Klystron Cavities
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The present paper examines how the resonance frequency f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>and the electrical Q factor relate to the geometrical shape of the coaxial insert in reentrant klystron cavities. Through proper selection of the geometry of the coaxial conductor (either circular cylinders or truncated cones), a tuning coefficient as high as 1.0 GHz/μm can be obtained at resonance frequencies around 10.0 GHz.

articleTitle: Small-Sized High Voltage Vacuum Triode GMI 30/25
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: We present vacuum metal-ceramic electron beam triode GMI 30/25 with high slope of the grid characteristic, wide intervals of admitted values of the grid current, cut-off voltage and heater power, the long service life. This tube continues series of high reliable pulsed triodes with short start time for use in wide class of microwave devices with grid control. The device consists of arc plasma oxide cathode of cylindrical form, molybdenum coaxial grid with longitudinal slots placed at the distance 400 mum from the emitter, and copper anode with radiator. Triode produces pulsed anode current up to 30 A, pulse length up to 50 musec. To decrease grid current the cathode has spacers without emission cover made between emitters, which serve as focusing electrodes

articleTitle: Study on the Impedance Matching of a Coaxial Marx Generator with a Field Emission Limited Diode
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The impedance matching between the coaxial Marx generator and the beam diode is investigated by using SPICE model simulations. By changing the value of the resistive load, the impedance of the coaxial Marx generator can be determined and by employing the analog behavioral modeling (ABM) of the diode in the SPICE simulation, the I-V characteristics of the high voltage diode driven by the coaxial Marx generator can be studied. The output voltage waveform, V-t curve, of the high voltage diode driven by the coaxial Marx generator and the corresponding output current waveform, I-t curve, can be calculated efficiently..

articleTitle: Computer Aided Design of Ka-band Waveguide Hybrid Junctions for Power Combining Architectures in Interplanetary Spacecraft
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: NASA's Prometheus program proposes using nuclear fission to provide unprecedented power capabilities for future interplanetary missions. Through nuclear fission, we can consider power-combining techniques using multiple TWTAs as opposed to multiple solid-state devices. Waveguide architectures represent one method of combining the power of multiple TWTAs and the fundamental element of waveguide combining architectures is the hybrid junction. We present the simulated transmission characteristics of four waveguide hybrid junctions designed for use in a TWTA power combining system capable of producing a kW of power.

articleTitle: Investigation of Synchronization and Transition to Chaos in a Driven TWT Delayed Feedback Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: A chaotic waveform generator based on a TWT amplifier with delayed recirculated feedback driven with an external harmonic signal has been developed. In this paper, a numerical model of the oscillator is described and results of numerical and experimental investigation are presented Such as oscillator is of great interest for novel communication and radar systems utilizing noise-like waveform signals.

articleTitle: Investigation of W-Band Folded Waveguide Slow-Wave Structure using MAFIA
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: MAFIA has been used in the simulation and optimization of TWT slow wave structure, and also the beam/wave interaction in helix TWT with fairly good accuracy. In this paper, a preliminary and quick design of W-band folded waveguide slow wave structure (FWG SWS) was performed based on theoretical research. The geometric and beam parameters optimization were carried out until all requirements were satisfied

articleTitle: Design of a 600-to-1200 kW Peak-Power, 50 % Duty L-Band Magnetron
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The design procedure for a high average power magnetron is described. High efficiency conversion of DC to RF power is a key goal. The use of particle-in-cell and finite element codes is described.

articleTitle: A General Thermal-Field Emission Equation
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: A general emission equation, which contains as its asymptotic limits both the Richardson (thermal emission) and the Fowler Nordheim (field emission) equations, is developed. The general thermal-field equation performs over a range of temperatures, fields, and work function values where the asymptotes are degraded

articleTitle: High Power Aluminum Nitride RF Vacuum Window
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: A window constructed from AlN was previously tested at high RF power using an S-band klystron. The experiment showed that the loss tangent of the AlN disc was much higher (0.003) than the value for an individual crystal (0.0005). The large loss tangent negated the advantages of its high thermal conductivity, resulting in a temperature rise across the window comparable to alumina

articleTitle: High Dimension Chaotic Attractors in Gyrotron with Non-Fixed Field Structure
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: In this paper we discuss results of numerical investigation of chaotic dynamics in Gyrotron with non-fixed field structure. We compute Lyapunov exponents for chaotic attractors and estimate their dimensions on the base of Kaplan-Yorke formula. Dimension values are found to be anomalously high and we correlate this result with the presence of large number of high-Q eigenmodes in gyrotron resonator due to operation near the cutoff frequency

articleTitle: Terahertz Smith-Purcell Radiation from Surface Plasmon Wave in One-Dimensional Photonic Crystal Structure using Counter-Streaming Electron Beam
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: A new THz Smith-Purcell radiation (SPR) free electron laser (FEL) using counter-streaming electron beams (CSEBs) on a one-dimensionally structured metal slab is introduced. The analytical dispersion curve and the calculated SPR-intensity of the CSEBs-SPR system explain how plasmon-transmissions between the CSEBs lower the tansition-threshold from a spontaneous emission to a stimulated one as well as enhance the radiation intensity. The self-frequency-locking effect of the system is verified by numerical simulations based on particle-in-cell (PIC) computation. On summary of the numerical analyses, the transition-threshold of CSEBs-SPR is lowered down to 2-3% of a conventional SPR. The radiation intensity of the former is about two orders of magnitude larger than that of the latter at the same beam-current density

articleTitle: Operation of a 95 GHz 100 kW Gyrotron in a High-Tc(BSCCO) Magnet
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Results of simulation and testing of a gyrotron in a high-temperature superconducting magnet are described. The high-temperature magnet was designed as a replacement for an existing low-temperature magnet. Magnetic materials were incorporated into the high-temperature magnet's cryostat, in order to achieve the fringing field profile required for compatibility with the gyrotron. Nevertheless, the shape of the original magnetic field profile could not be precisely matched, resulting in an 8% reduction in gyrotron efficiency. Magnet cooling power requirements were reduced by a factor of two, and charging time was reduced by a factor of 30

articleTitle: Hollow Cathode Life Issues
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: L-3 Communications ETI (formerly Boeing Electron Dynamics Division and, prior to that, a division of Hughes Space and Communications) is a company with significant background in both cathodes (used in space traveling wave tubes) and electric propulsion. L-3 ETI has been responsible for developing a cathode life model as presented in R. T. Longo (2003) that is recognized throughout the industry and has also been a key enabler in the development and manufacture of gridded ion thrusters. Testing of the 25 cm xenon ion propulsion system (XIPS) has demonstrated 2 potential ignition issues associated with the hollow cathode assembly: delayed ignition due to barium depletion and heater failure. In its role in satellite station-keeping, the XIPS engine is ignited daily over a 15 year mission so that a detailed understanding of the ignition process is important in evaluating its life. The heater used to ignite the XIPS cathode assembly represents a single point failure so that dealing with potential failure mechanisms is critical in ensuring mission life

articleTitle: Phase Variant CFA Study
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The phase length of a crossed-field amplifier (CFA) depends primarily on the dimensions of the anode vanes. CPI/BMD has studied the relationship of individual vane components for a typical CFA, the SFD-262. The vane structure can be reduced to four separate sections, the vane stub, body, tip, and advance. The vane-to-vane capacitance and inductance were modeled analytically to produce phase sensitivity functions. After selecting component dimensions the RF behavior of the vanes is modeled with an electromagnetic code (HFSS). The resulting dispersion relationship was then compared to the dispersion in a series of CFA's that have been constructed. The dispersion relationship was measured on a rotary table

articleTitle: The Growth of Layer-by-Layer Aligned Carbon Nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: Ferrocene as catalyst precursor, layer-by-layer vertically aligned carbon nanotubes were grown on silicon substrates using chemical vapor deposition (CVD) by decomposing acetylene twice. The SEM images showed that the intervals of the twice introduction of acetylene is a crucial factor for the interface combination of carbon nanotubes layers. Maybe we can use this interval to introduce something else to form a new layer between the two carbon nanotubes layers to synthesize new functional nano-composites.

articleTitle: A Study of Macroscopic Emission Non-Uniformity in Thermionic Cathodes Due to Profilimetry Variation
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: We develop a model to show that the micron-scale ridges due to surface machining of thermionic dispenser cathodes may cause significant angular variations in the macroscopic current density on ring-shaped cathodes as are commonly used in gyrotrons. The local field enhancement caused by the ridges resulting from machining gives an angular variation in current that may be pronounced. An explanation in terms of wobble of the cathode during machining and the eccentricity of the cathode cross-section can explain much of the observed variation

articleTitle: The Composite Pyramidal-Rectangular Resonator for Microwave Dryer
publicationTitle: 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electronics Conference held Jointly with 2006 IEEE International Vacuum Electron Sources
abstract: The results of pyramidal-rectangular resonator for microwave dryer simulation are present.
